editorial:
Ever wonder how the biggest secrets of the government actually get leaked? You get a front-row seat to that world here. The film follows Seymour Hersh, a legendary journalist who spent his whole life hunting down the truth. It feels less like a dry history lesson and more like a spy thriller. You see him tackle massive scandals like the My Lai massacre and the horrors of Abu Ghraib, showing you exactly how he tracked down sources and pressured people in power to stop lying. The vibe is intense and gritty, making you feel the pressure he faced while risking everything for a story.

What really works is the pacing; it never feels slow because the stakes are always so high. You will love the old footage and the way the interviews are handled, though some of the political details might feel a bit heavy if you aren't into history. If you enjoy true crime or political drama, you need to see this.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up by showing Hersh in his later years, still fighting to expose the truth even when the world has moved on. The final scenes reveal that his battle isn't just about one story, but about the principle of holding leaders accountable. It ends with a powerful message that the truth always finds a way out eventually, leaving you to think about who is controlling the news today.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves real-life mysteries and political scandals.
